subject.title: Omission-resistant product completeness and closure currentness

semantics.desiredOutcome: Product readiness and closure are evaluated only from one canonical complete current product-history subject plus canonical acceptance-policy authority, so callers cannot manufacture ELIGIBLE_FOR_CLOSURE by omitting blocking claims, obligations, stale subjects or newer product transitions.
semantics.currentState: The delivered system and queued Integration C through E/F semantics do not yet provide ProductHistoryHead, a canonical product-level completeness boundary, a deterministic rebuildable ProductStateProjection, or a currentness-safe ProductOutcomeClaim closure path.

requiredBehaviors.statement: Closure-relevant product transitions are recorded as immutable append-only product history and advance one CAS-fenced ProductHistoryHead that commits to one complete ordered history prefix.

Every closure-relevant semantic claim, obligation, accepted-lineage, deployment/quality acceptance, root/objective/outcome, and applicable policy/waiver currentness transition participates in the canonical product-history commit boundary before it can affect closure semantics.
Per-subject semantic claim and obligation heads remain usable operational indexes, but product closure cannot treat a caller-selected or ad hoc scan of those heads as completeness proof.

A trusted projection builder consumes an exact ProductHistoryHead and exact current acceptance-policy authority and derives the complete current closure subject; callers cannot supply a subset of current claims, obligations, blockers or waivers to define readiness.

The projection builder produces an immutable ProductProjectionSubject that pins exact history generation/digest, root intent/outcome/objective refs, acceptance policy revision, derived applicable waiver refs and projection algorithm version.
ProductStateProjection is a deterministic disposable derived view; deleting it and rebuilding from the same ProductProjectionSubject yields the same readiness and blocker set.

An authorized closure action can publish an immutable ProductOutcomeClaim only after revalidating the exact ProductHistoryHead and acceptance-policy subject used by the eligible projection immediately before closure commit.
If product history or policy currentness changes after projection but before closure, the old projection is stale and closure fails closed until rebuilt.
A ProductOutcomeClaim remains immutable historical evidence; later closure-relevant history may make it non-current without rewriting the historical claim or silently preserving a permanent DONE bit.
Post-closure supersession derives a new current projection and materializes only bounded revalidation/remediation required by the changed semantic lineage instead of resetting the whole organization.

invariants.statement: Caller-selected current refs are not completeness proof.
ProductHistoryHead is a product-completeness/currentness subject, not an organization scheduler, execution log or observability stream.
ProductStateProjection is not product authority and is never directly mutated as truth.
A stable product state cannot expose a newer authoritative closure-relevant transition while the canonical completeness head still commits only to an older state.
Historical ProductOutcomeClaim is not a permanent current DONE bit.
Acceptance-policy and applicable-waiver currentness are derived from canonical authority and pinned in the projection subject rather than accepted as a convenient caller subset.
Execution-policy or execution-strategy changes alone do not change product readiness unless accepted product semantic lineage changes.

Cryptographic Merkle inclusion/consistency proofs are not required for Integration G v1; exact generation/digest commitment and durable CAS/recovery are sufficient for the current trusted-store threat model.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Omitting a current QUALITY_REJECTED claim from caller input cannot make the product eligible; the builder derives it from canonical history and returns NOT_READY.
Omitting a current blocking obligation from caller input cannot make the product eligible; the builder derives the obligation and returns NOT_READY.
A projection built at history head Hn cannot authorize closure after a closure-relevant Hn+1 transition; the closure currentness recheck rejects the stale basis.
Deleting any cached ProductStateProjection and rebuilding from the same pinned subject yields identical readiness, active-set identity and blockers.
Restarting a fresh process can reconstruct the same current product subject and projection from durable history/policy refs without prior conversation state.
Changing acceptance-policy revision while product history is unchanged makes the old projection subject non-current and requires deterministic re-evaluation.

Publishing a new accepted Backend or other closure-relevant product revision after closure retains the old ProductOutcomeClaim historically but makes current readiness re-evaluate under the newer history head.
Attempted in-place mutation of an historical claim, obligation, history commit or ProductOutcomeClaim is rejected; correction occurs through new immutable transitions.
A strategy-only revision with unchanged accepted product outputs and lineage does not by itself invalidate product closure readiness.

outOfScope.statement: Global organization scheduling, role sequencing or next-domain dispatch.
Generic event-sourcing platform, universal provenance database or organization-wide telemetry ledger.
Mandatory Certificate Transparency, Merkle-tree inclusion proofs or external transparency-log infrastructure.
Implementation of terminal Blackboard DONE reopening; Integration G v1 uses immutable historical closure plus current projection/revalidation semantics.
Adversarial recovery benchmark, causal observability and self-improvement loops reserved for later Integration H through J.
